# PLAGUE and FALLOW contact observations

`plague_fallow.tsv` records actual original `touchEffects2` calls for PLAGUE and FALLOW attacking segments.
Two source runs and the bundled JAR produce identical bytes.
All five compiled helper classes also match across both backends.
The corpus contains 395 cases, 1187 snapshots, 792 explicit operations, and 108 actual newborns.

## Comparison contract

This contract and the complete row ledger precede Rust replay.
Compare scalar, photo, gas, statistics, velocity, endpoint, color, reaction, identity, and RNG observations exactly.
Only organism fields `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the existing geometry allowance.
For finite geometry values, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Check geometric NaN classification and signed infinity explicitly.
No other floating tolerance or NaN substitution applies.
Preserve signed zero and complete 32-bit ARGB values.
Immutable Java Color reference identity maps to exact ARGB value semantics.

Only `input` G/N blocks and labelled construction recipes supply original genomes.
Explicit U and I records supply source globals and controlled runtime inputs.
Never construct newborns or replacement objects from later observations.
Discover newborns through actual object identity, including duplicate and wrapped numeric IDs.
Keep genotype identities through actors, newborns, saved references, and synchronous statistics.

## Source authority

The PLAGUE branch occupies `Organism.java:14142-14940`.
Its catalog identity is `JAVA-Organism-CASE-14142-1`.
The FALLOW branch occupies `Organism.java:14941-15861`.
Its catalog identity is `JAVA-Organism-CASE-14941-1`.
The common recipient-energy death guard occupies `Organism.java:17917-17919`.
Its catalog identity is `JAVA-Organism-IF-17917-1`.

The helper invokes the actual private `touchEffects2(Organism,int,int)` through reflection.
Before each call, it requires the labelled attacking segment's exact current ARGB.
Nested reproduction, inheritance, payment, neutralization, inhibition, restoration, death, statistics, and placement calls remain original source calls.
The helper does not copy those methods into an expected-state calculator.

Viral births execute `reproduceVirus` at `Organism.java:4021-4082`.
Foreign births execute `reproduceforeignVirus` at `Organism.java:4091-4156`.
The saved-genome priority in `inherit` remains observable at `Organism.java:1972-1978`.

## Execution and inputs

Compile `tools/reference/PlagueFallowOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.PlagueFallowOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` using the isolated profile arguments recorded in provenance.
The helper requires isolated home, temporary, and both preferences roots before simulation access.
It rejects an existing output directory and writes the TSV with `CREATE_NEW`.
The existing runner bounds each process and cleans only its owned process group.
No GUI launch, network operation, original modification, or global profile change is required.

Each case resets source defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive settings.
`INITIAL_ORGANISMS` is zero, and initial oxygen is `1000`.
Other initial gases retain source defaults.
Mutation bounds are `0..10000`, and meta mutation is zero.
GREEN weight is seven; the other 45 selectable weights are zero.
The initial seed is `827364`.
Explicit U and I records identify every override.

The ordinary PLAGUE cost is `1.25`, and the SCOURGE cost is `0.25`.
The FALLOW cost is `0.125`, and the dodge cost is `0.5`.
The BLUE cost is `0.75`, and the MAGENTA cost is `0.375`.
Separate cases supply INDIGO costs `0` and `0.5`, and a LAVENDER cost of zero.
These are deliberate source-global inputs, even when provisional Rust public validation rejects them.
Original World construction does not inspect these costs at `World.java:391-399`.
The Rust method harness must install exact supplied settings before actor construction.
These observations do not establish complete preferences or settings-import compatibility.

Five supplied genomes use identities `g0` through `g4`.
Recipes for `g0..g3` are explicit; `g4` uses actual `GeneticCode.clone()` on `g0`.
`g0` supplies the attacker, `g1` the recipient, and `g2` a separate selector/blocker.
`g3` supplies an independent WHITE infection code.
The full input G/N blocks record every supplied property and gene field.
Most peer colors change current phenotype independently from the recipient's GREEN genotype.

Three real organisms are pasted and added in selector, victim, killer order.
The selector occupies `(1000,1000)`, the attacker `(3500,3500)`, and the recipient `(5000,5000)`.
Protocol role `victim` names the attacker; role `killer` names the recipient.
Role `selector` names the independent blocker and selected organism.
A real separate selector avoids MainWindow callbacks.
Selection remains an explicit source-only metadata exclusion.

`build_tree` creates a real frozen JTS tree from an explicit current-member role list.
J records actual insertion bounds; Q records actual query order.
Newborns enter the real world list without entering the existing frozen tree.
Two cases explicitly rebuild that tree after a controlled shared-gene edit.
Contacts use attacking segment zero, except one FALLOW case using segment one.
The recipient segment is always zero.

The 792 operations comprise 397 tree builds, 208 PLAGUE calls, and 187 FALLOW calls.
They discover 108 actual newborn objects through world-list identity.
Blocked placement inserts no newborn and preserves the actual failed-attempt side effects.
Internal failed candidates are not invented or retained for observation.

The original 381 cases deliberately supply saved genotype `g4` to the recipient.
All 96 newborns from that prefix reuse that exact saved object.
The case named `plague-full-mutation-birth` therefore demonstrates saved priority, despite its input mutation rate.
It does not prove an inheritance mutation occurred.

Fourteen appended cases remove the saved reference before the actual source call.
These preserve all original 381 case bytes exactly.
They add unsaved viral/foreign births, blocked placement, full mutation, spore variants, ID wrapping, and shared-gene edits.
Successful unsaved births discover genotype `g5` with generation `42`.
Both full-mutation cases change actual gene data and append the actual lineage suffix `root>3`.
Blocked unsaved attempts retain actual `g5` through the recipient's saved reference.
That retained reference is observable and remains a comparison obligation.
The shared-gene edit changes both `g0` and inherited `g5`, while their clade strings remain distinct.

## Protocol and scope

Use the [shared dynamic TSV protocol](reproduction.README.md#shared-tsv-protocol).
The mode is `plague-fallow`.
K contact rows contain stage, `touchEffects2.PLAGUE` or `touchEffects2.FALLOW`, `victim`, and `killer,segment,0`.
K tree rows contain stage, `build_tree`, `victim`, and the explicit inserted role list.
There are no Z direct-candidate rows.

Each actor snapshot contains all 154 organism fields and three genotype-reference holders.
Each world snapshot contains ten getter-style values and all 15 instance fields.
Each statistics snapshot contains all 52 fields and 49 public zero-argument getters.
Each genome observation contains 28 fields, including synthetic reference and gene-count fields.
Every observed gene contains all 40 source fields.
R records the following long, bounded integer, and raw double from a copied source Random.
R inspection does not advance the live simulation generator.

D binds newborns through actual world-list object identities.
H and G preserve actual genotype references, including shared, saved, inherited, mutated, and statistics-rooted references.
Y retains the existing `observable` and `rejected-only` meanings.
All 5950 Y records are `observable`; no rejected-only genotype rows occur.
No observed newborn fields or post-call genotype records become construction input.

O `_world` and `_visibleWorld` remain named collaborator exclusions.
V `_visibleWorld`, `inCorridors`, `outCorridors`, and `_corridorexists` remain named UI or corridor exclusions.
These fields do not prove implemented UI callbacks or transport.
All other fields, observable genotypes, identities, queries, statistics, and RNG observations remain comparisons.
